title: Where is the robot?
summary: Pose estimation, and why it drifts from the truth.

say.never:
A **pose** is a robot's position on the field (x and y) *and* which way it's facing. The pose estimator works it out by adding up every tiny movement of the wheels, like counting your steps to guess how far you walked.

Start at (x 0, y 0) facing east. Drive 1 m forward and you are at (x 1, y 0), still facing east. Turn left and drive 1 m and you are at (x 1, y 1), facing north.
say.bit: A pose is x, y and heading, built by adding up many small wheel movements.

say.never:
The pose estimator needs two moves every loop. First feed it the latest movement, then ask where it thinks the robot is and keep the answer:

`poseEstimator.update(getYaw(), getLeftMeters(), getRightMeters());`

`pose = poseEstimator.getEstimatedPosition();`
say.bit: Feed it the latest movement with `poseEstimator.update(getYaw(), getLeftMeters(), getRightMeters());`, then store `poseEstimator.getEstimatedPosition()` in `pose`.

say.never:
Inside `updatePose()` the TODO comment shows what to write. Add this line below it (you can delete the comment lines when you are done):

`poseEstimator.update(getYaw(), getLeftMeters(), getRightMeters());`

This hands the estimator the heading from `getYaw()` and how far each side has driven. It runs every loop, so the estimator keeps adding up the movement.
say.bit: Under the TODO, write `poseEstimator.update(getYaw(), getLeftMeters(), getRightMeters());`.

say.never:
Now ask the estimator where the robot is and keep the answer in the `pose` variable. Add this line under the first one:

`pose = poseEstimator.getEstimatedPosition();`

`getPose()` hands this variable to the rest of the robot and to the logs.
